architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk

planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged isothermal melt residence at 120 C (thermal-hold drift).
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 thermal-hold run increased by 51.54% from 15 to 60 min and by 93.08% from 15 to 90 min at 120 C, compared with 9.51% and 16.85%, respectively, for E1.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only one 120 C hold trajectory is available for each of E1 and E5, with four points over 15-90 min, and no hold trajectory is reported for the E2 reactive-core anchor or for any acrylic-only versus tackifier-containing matched comparison. In contrast, temperature response is measured at six temperatures from 80 to 130 C across multiple formulations and runs, and realized viscosity-level variability is directly documented for E2 by three-run spreads of approximately 2.80-3.57-fold.
measurement_requirements: Use the matched-window 120 C hold protocol, measuring viscosity at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min and reporting SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 as a percentage.
Run at least two independent preparations under controlled and fully recorded process histories so thermal drift is not interpreted from a single realization.
Measure and retain the 15 min viscosity as the realized viscosity-level anchor rather than comparing drift without documenting the starting state.

Before observing results, calculate the candidate's reactive mass fraction and freeze the H-CORE prediction E1_drift times phi_r, the H-RESIN threshold of less than half that prediction, and the 2 percentage-point discrimination threshold.
Use an acrylic-only candidate with zero minor tackifier for the primary mechanistic test so that low drift can directly test H-DUAL's tackifier-required prediction.
Keep the hold temperature and 15-60 min decision window inside the locally measured support; do not extrapolate beyond the observed temperature or time ranges.
Preserve source viscosity units as unknown unless independently established, and base the primary comparison on dimensionless matched-window relative drift.
planner.scientific_question: For an acrylic-modified, zero-tackifier formulation built on the E2 reactive-core anchor, is the matched-window 120 C viscosity drift consistent with linear dilution of the E1 reference, or is it less than half that prediction? A drift below half the linear-dilution prediction would separate H-RESIN from H-CORE and would also falsify H-DUAL's requirement for a non-zero minor tackifier; drift near the linear prediction would reject superlinear suppression for that composition.

hypotheses_not_separated: H-CORE from H-DUAL: both predict approximately linear-dilution drift for an acrylic-only, zero-tackifier composition

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: For reactive mass fraction phi_r = 0.80, the frozen H-CORE prediction is 9.51% x 0.80 = 7.608%, and the H-RESIN acceptance threshold is SI_15_60 < 3.804%. A repeat-confirmed result below 3.804% supports superlinear resin suppression over linear dilution, falsifies H-CORE for this composition, and falsifies H-DUAL because the low-drift regime was reached with zero minor tackifier.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: SI_15_60 >= 7.608% falsifies H-RESIN for this composition. A result within 2 percentage points of 7.608% supports H-CORE within the declared measurement resolution and is consistent with H-DUAL, but it cannot distinguish H-CORE from H-DUAL. A result more than 2 percentage points above 7.608% rejects H-RESIN but does not positively support the quantitative H-CORE prediction.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result from 3.804% to below 7.608% does not meet either the strong H-RESIN acceptance threshold or its formal falsification threshold. Values below 5.608% are more than the 2-point resolution below the linear prediction and therefore falsify H-CORE without reaching the registered strong-suppression criterion; values from 5.608% to below 7.608% remain resolution-consistent with H-CORE. H-DUAL is not positively established by this single acrylic-only experiment unless a tackifier-containing comparison later shows low drift selectively.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, during a 120 C hold

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: The 15% acrylic-only hold is a smaller intervention and has adequate prediction separation, but its literature loading is retained only as directional lower-bound evidence because the fraction denominator is not verified as directly commensurate.

The 25% acrylic-only hold is directly supported and has relevant 121 C stability analogue evidence, but it is a larger perturbation than necessary and gives a slightly smaller gap between the linear and half-linear thresholds.

The 20% acrylic plus 5% tackifier hold lies within supported regions and could test mitigation, but the dual-axis intervention confounds modifier attribution and cannot falsify H-DUAL through low drift in the absence of tackifier.
It measures a fitted temperature-response descriptor rather than the declared thermal-hold failure mode, so it neither directly observes SI_15_60 nor adjudicates the registered drift thresholds.
It directly characterizes preparation-state spread but answers process repeatability rather than the formulation-level hot-hold mechanism.

proposer.reasoning: S1C49 uses 20% acrylic and zero tackifier, placing the intervention at a directly commensurate acrylic evidence anchor and within the conservative 15-20% initial-test band. The direct matched-window hold observable addresses the least-resolved coordinate without regression, extrapolation, or model-based imputation. Its 3.804-percentage-point gap between the linear and half-linear predictions exceeds the declared 2-point discrimination threshold. At least two independently prepared, process-history-controlled repeats should be run, with the 15-minute viscosity retained as the realization-state anchor. No deterministic VOI ranking or tied top set was supplied.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Replace the immediate S1C49 acrylic-only hold with an E2 reactive-core-only matched-window 120 C hold using at least two independent, process-history-controlled preparations. Use the resulting E2 drift coefficient, with a preregistered repeat aggregation and uncertainty rule, to define the later S1C49 linear-dilution prediction. S1C01 is selected as the canonical inventory entry among apparently composition-identical reactive-core-only candidates.
robustness_adjudication.departure_from_deterministic_ranking: Membership cannot be established because the deterministic VOI score, ranking, tied_top_experiment_ids, top_experiment_set_stability, base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower, and recommendation_flip_boundary were withheld. The adjudicated change is therefore not a preference-based override of a known ranking; it is scientifically justified by the missing E2 core-only hold coefficient identified in the Skeptic's strongest objection.
residual_decision_risk: The preferred E2 control does not itself discriminate H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL; a subsequent acrylic-only hold remains necessary.
The inventory contains multiple apparently identical reactive-core-only candidates, and no supplied metadata distinguishes S1C01 from S1C02 through S1C09.

E2 shows approximately 2.80-3.57-fold between-preparation viscosity-scale variation, so process history, the 15-minute anchor, repeat aggregation, and uncertainty treatment must be controlled prospectively.
The acrylic modifier's OH or other NCO-reactive functionality remains unverified; true stoichiometry and reactive mass fraction must be recalculated before interpreting S1C49.
Without a verified non-reactive diluent control matched to the same reactive mass fraction, a later deviation from linear dilution cannot uniquely establish resin-specific suppression.
H-DUAL lacks a preregistered numerical definition of the low-drift regime.
The direct hold observable cannot establish the molecular encounter-frequency explanation stated for H-RESIN.
No decision-stability quantities were supplied, so robustness to VOI re-weighting and any tied-top-set structure remain unknown.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: S1C49::M-HOLD-120 directly measures the relevant drift observable, but its central 7.608% comparator applies the single-run E1 drift coefficient to an E2-based formulation. Because no E2 core-only hold trajectory exists, the proposed experiment cannot securely distinguish E2-specific linear dilution from superlinear suppression. The next experiment should therefore measure the process-matched E2 reactive-core-only hold response before testing S1C49. This changes the experiment to run now, rather than merely limiting interpretation after the proposed run.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: No weight-sensitivity assessment is possible from the supplied payload. The decision-stability report states deterministic_rule_layer_withheld and decision_stability_withheld, so no perturbation that changes the tied top set, and no scientific defensibility of such a weighting, can be identified.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: M-HOLD-120 directly measures SI_15_60 and can numerically return a value at or above 7.608%, so the stated H-RESIN falsification event is physically attainable. Practical adjudication is incomplete because the proposal does not define how the two or more repeats are combined, and scientific interpretation remains compromised by the unmeasured E2 baseline and unverified acrylic inertness.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result below 3.804% could show low drift relative to an E1-derived benchmark, but it could not establish superlinear suppression relative to the E2 core or falsify an E2-specific linear-dilution prediction.
objections.objection: The frozen H-CORE prediction of 7.608% is calculated from E1_drift_15_60_pct = 9.51%, but S1C49 is built on the E2 reactive-core anchor. The planner explicitly states that no E2 hold trajectory exists, and E2 has NCO:OH = 1.80 while E1 is a different original formulation. Therefore, the experiment does not know the undiluted drift coefficient of the reactive core actually used in S1C49. In addition, the 9.51% E1 reference comes from one run, so its uncertainty is not included in the claimed 3.804-percentage-point separation from the half-linear threshold.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment could falsify the tackifier-required clause only under a post hoc or borrowed definition of "low," weakening the claimed H-RESIN-versus-H-DUAL separation.
objections.objection: H-DUAL uses the terms "low drift" and "low-drift regime" without a registered numerical boundary. The proposer implicitly equates SI_15_60 < 3.804% with low drift when claiming that this result falsifies H-DUAL, but that threshold is registered for H-RESIN rather than H-DUAL.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Any departure from 7.608% cannot be uniquely attributed to the registered H-RESIN mechanism of resin-specific superlinear suppression; altered stoichiometry, acrylic reactivity, ordinary dilution, or other acrylic-induced state changes remain available explanations.
objections.objection: The 20% acrylic intervention simultaneously changes acrylic identity, reactive-core mass fraction, realized viscosity level, and potentially reactive stoichiometry. The E2 inspection explicitly warns that true stoichiometry must be recalculated if the modifier contributes OH or another NCO-reactive group, yet phi_r = 0.80 is treated as reaction-capable mass fraction without supplied verification that the acrylic is chemically inert. No matched 20% verified-inert diluent control is included.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No direct-observable claim is lost, but direct measurement of SI_15_60 should not be conflated with validity of the E1-derived mechanistic comparator.
objections.objection: The primary observable itself survives this attack: SI_15_60 is calculated directly from measured eta_15 and eta_60 at 120 C and requires no regression, extrapolation, or imputation. The weakness lies in the external prediction benchmark, not in reading the observable.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Borderline or discordant repeats cannot be adjudicated prospectively, and the nominal threshold may support different conclusions depending on an unstated aggregation rule.
objections.objection: The numerical H-RESIN falsification event, SI_15_60 >= 7.608%, can be produced by the specified measurement. However, the protocol says to run at least two repeats while the interpretation requires a "repeat-confirmed" result without defining whether both repeats must cross the threshold, whether their mean is used, or how disagreement and uncertainty are handled. The declared 2-percentage-point resolution also does not incorporate uncertainty in the single-run E1 reference.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low-drift result would be overinterpreted as evidence for a specific encounter-frequency mechanism rather than evidence for phenomenological suppression in this formulation.
objections.objection: No target outcome leakage is evident in the supplied proposal. However, M-HOLD-120 can establish only formulation-level drift and deviations from a specified dilution prediction. It cannot establish H-RESIN's stated causal explanation that suppression occurs by "lowering the effective concentration and encounter frequency of reaction-capable species within a non-reactive continuum," especially because modifier inertness is not independently verified.

skeptic.recommended_change: Run a concurrent, process-matched E2 reactive-core-only M-HOLD-120 control with the same repeat count and replace E1_drift in the frozen H-CORE prediction with the measured E2 drift. Verify the acrylic's OH or other NCO-reactive functionality and recalculate true stoichiometry before defining phi_r. If resin-specific suppression rather than merely failure of a mathematical dilution rule is claimed, add a composition matched to phi_r = 0.80 using a verified non-reactive diluent. Also preregister the repeat aggregation rule, uncertainty treatment, and a numerical definition of H-DUAL's low-drift regime.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The experiment applies the single-run E1 drift coefficient to an E2-based candidate without measuring the E2 core-only hold response. Consequently, the frozen 7.608% linear-dilution prediction is not a validated prediction for the reactive core actually under test, so the central H-CORE-versus-H-RESIN discrimination is not securely identified.

design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.
